defects.summary: CAPABILITIES.md claimed 'auth + owner-scoped' for ALL entities; low-sensitivity domains actually generate PUBLIC CRUD
defects.fix: tools/eos.py policy_label() derives the claim from gen_models.effective_policies; regression in tests/security_regression.py

defects.summary: data_sensitivity 'low' generates anonymous create/update/DELETE (anon POST /tools -> 201, anon DELETE -> 204) — bad default for 'basic_saas'
defects.fix: recommended: public reads, auth writes at low tier

defects.summary: create accepts arbitrary values for state-machine fields (row created in a state not in the machine), breaking reference rules downstream
defects.fix: recommended: force initial state or validate against machine states on create

defects.summary: shared (auth-only) entities are writable/deletable by ANY authenticated user (sobriety Meeting/Sponsor, healthcare Encounter)
defects.fix: recommended: role-gate writes on shared entities in domain specs

defects.summary: RIGHT-TO-ERASURE DID NOT ERASE IDENTITY: generated /privacy/delete-account called delete_account() without confirm=True -> silent dry-run; route returned {'deleted': true}; deleted account could LOG BACK IN. Registry prose claimed 'proven end-to-end' with no executable backing
defects.fix: gen_models emits confirm=True; verify_runtime --fullstack now proves erasure (session revoked, re-login 401, bystander intact) — 12/12

defects.summary: DeletionRecord table never created (account_deletion imported lazily inside route, model missed boot-time create_all) — hard-delete path crashed at commit once F5 was fixed
defects.fix: module-scope import in generated routes + account_deletion in security_caps + table in _ensure_security_tables

defects.summary: billing/subscription parts materialize as library code but NO billing routes are generated (openapi has zero billing surface); live Stripe SDK path also unwired (documented)
defects.fix: recommended: generate checkout/subscription routes when billing caps resolve

defects.summary: DSAR EXPORT LEAKED CREDENTIALS: /privacy/export contained argon2 password hash AND the live plaintext session token (account takeover from a leaked export file)
defects.fix: data_export redacts SECRET_COLUMNS; selftest + security_regression cover hash+token

defects.summary: EOS path wrote no deployment artifacts (Dockerfile/compose only on template path) despite resolving the 'docker' capability
account_deletion declared internal scrapyard modules as pip dependencies -> generated requirements.txt uninstallable -> Docker builds failed
defects.fix: metadata corrected + assemble_parts filters scrapyard.* from pip deps

defects.summary: 197/582 parts import third-party modules they never declare; apps only installed because SOME OTHER part declared the package (httpx broke c-saas/marketplace/healthcare containers)
defects.fix: assemble_parts scans copied sources (AST, module-level imports) and unions known pip names into requirements; password_policy metadata corrected

defects.summary: gen_frontend_react emitted absolute asset base '/', but EOS mounts the SPA at /app/ -> built assets 404 in the browser
hardening_registry 'proven end-to-end' prose claims are not executable evidence (the erasure claim was false through the HTTP route)
defects.fix: recommended: registry entries should reference executable checks

defects.summary: GENERATED SPA RENDERED AS A BLANK PAGE IN EVERY REAL BROWSER: the backend's own Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self') blocks the SPA's inline <style>/<script>. Every verifier (repo's and campaign's) passed because nothing executed JS — found only when a human opened the page
defects.fix: gen_frontend now emits external styles.css + app.js (CSP-compliant; JSON config block stays inline as data); proven by headless-Edge post-JS DOM dump; structural regression in security_regression.py

defects.summary: template-path (assemble) pages ship WITHOUT the security headers the EOS path enforces, and depend on the Tailwind CDN (offline = unstyled)
defects.fix: recommended: unify header middleware across paths; vendor the CSS
